subject: math
title: Time: Seconds, Minutes and Hours, O’clock and Half Past, How Long Things Take
seo_title: Grade 2 Time Math Worksheets: Seconds, Minutes, Hours and Half Past, Free with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Use units of time, including seconds, minutes, hours, and non-standard units, to describe the duration of various events
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on time for the Ontario curriculum: choose seconds, minutes or hours, compare longer and shorter events with sand timers, read clocks to the hour and half hour, find how long from start to end, and solve timer word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Seconds for quick things, minutes for a little while, hours for long things.
key_sub: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50. To find how long, count the jumps from the start time, not the numbers.
body_html:
Seconds, minutes and hours

We use units of time to tell how long something takes. Seconds are for very quick things. Minutes are for things that take a little while. Hours are for long things.

UnitGood forExample
secondsvery quick thingsclap 3 times: about 3 seconds
minutesthings that take a little whilebrush your teeth: about 2 minutes
hourslong thingssleep at night: about 10 hours

60 seconds = 1 minute. 60 minutes = 1 hour. Half an hour = 30 minutes.

Choose the unit

About how long is recess?

Recess is longer than a few seconds, but shorter than an hour.

Answer: about 15 minutes

Longer or shorter

We can also measure time with things like claps or a sand timer. Use the same sand timer each time. More sand timers means a longer time.

Look at the unit, not only the number. 3 minutes is longer than 30 seconds.

O’clock and half past

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. At o’clock, the long hand points to the 12. At half past, it points to the 6.

How long from start to end?

Start at the start time. Jump 1 hour at a time. Then jump half an hour if you need to. Count the jumps.

Timer

Recess is 15 minutes. 10 minutes have passed. How many minutes are left?

15 − 10 = 5

Answer: 5 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Brushing teeth takes 2 hoursQuick things take seconds or minutes. It takes about 2 minutes.
Half an hour is 50 minutes1 hour is 60 minutes, so half an hour is 30 minutes.
3 minutes is shorter than 30 seconds, because 3 is smallerLook at the unit. 3 minutes is 180 seconds.
Half past 3 read as half past 4The short hand has not reached the 4 yet. It is still 3.
3:00 to 5:00 is 3 hours (3, 4, 5)Count the jumps, not the numbers: 2 hours.

faq.q: What do Grade 2 students learn about time in Ontario math?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum (expectation E2.4), Grade 2 students use seconds, minutes, hours and non-standard units, like claps or a sand timer, to describe how long events last.

faq.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
faq.a: Half an hour is 30 minutes, because 1 hour is 60 minutes. Many children guess 50 minutes, because they think of 100 instead of 60.

faq.q: Do Grade 2 students learn to tell time to the minute?
faq.a: Not yet. In Grade 2, o’clock and half past help students say how long things take. In Grade 3, students use analog and digital clocks to tell time in hours, minutes and seconds.

faq.q: How can I help my child understand how long a minute is?
faq.a: Use a kitchen timer for everyday jobs, like brushing teeth for 2 minutes or tidying up for 5 minutes. Ask your child to guess first, then check with the timer.

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to blink your eyes?
items.e: It is over very fast, so we use seconds. (Not hours: an hour is much too long for that.)

items.q: About how long does it take to drink a cup of water?
items.e: A few big sips are quick. So it takes about 10 seconds. (Not 10 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to brush your teeth?
items.e: It takes longer than a few seconds, but much less than an hour. We use minutes.

items.q: About how long does it take to read a picture book?
items.e: You turn many pages, but it is much less than an hour. So it takes about 10 minutes. (Not 10 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to tie your shoes?
items.e: It is over very fast, so we use seconds. (Not hours: an hour is much too long for that.)

items.q: About how long does it take to clap your hands 3 times?
items.e: Clap, clap, clap: that is very quick. So it takes about 3 seconds. (Not 3 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to sleep at night?
items.e: It takes a long time, more than an hour. We use hours.

items.q: About how long does it take to drive from Toronto to Ottawa?
items.e: It is a long car ride, most of a day. So it takes about 5 hours. (Not 5 minutes: that is far too short.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long recess lasts?
items.e: It takes longer than a few seconds, but much less than an hour. We use minutes.

items.q: About how long does it take to put on snow pants, boots and mitts?
items.e: It takes a little while, but not an hour. So it takes about 5 minutes. (Not 5 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to watch a hockey game at the arena?
items.e: It takes a long time, more than an hour. We use hours.

items.q: About how long does it take to jump up and down 5 times?
items.e: Five jumps are over very fast. So it takes about 5 seconds. (Not 5 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to zip up your coat?
items.e: It is over very fast, so we use seconds. (Not hours: an hour is much too long for that.)

items.q: About how long does it take to take a bath?
items.e: A bath is longer than a few seconds, but much less than a day. So it takes about 20 minutes. (Not 20 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long a school day lasts?
items.e: It takes a long time, more than an hour. We use hours.

items.q: About how long does it take to go on a class field trip to the museum?
items.e: There is a lot to see, and the bus ride takes time too. So it takes about 3 hours. (Not 3 minutes: that is far too short.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long it takes to eat your breakfast?
items.e: It takes longer than a few seconds, but much less than an hour. We use minutes.

items.q: About how long does it take to bake a pan of cookies in the oven?
items.e: Cookies bake for a short time, not for hours. So it takes about 12 minutes. (Not 12 hours: that is far too long.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long March Break lasts?
items.e: It lasts for more than one whole day. We use days.

items.q: About how long does it take to have a family picnic at the lake?
items.e: Eating, swimming and playing take a long time. So it takes about 2 hours. (Not 2 minutes: that is far too short.)

items.q: Which takes longer?
items.e: Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes. Sleeping at night takes about 10 hours. So sleeping at night takes longer.

items.q: Which takes less time?
items.e: Tying your shoes takes seconds. A hockey game takes hours. So tying your shoes takes less time.

items.q: Which is longer: 1 minute or 1 hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. So 1 hour is much longer than 1 minute.

items.q: Which is shorter: 1 second or 1 minute?
items.e: 1 minute is 60 seconds. So 1 second is shorter.

items.q: Which takes longer?
items.e: Reading a picture book takes minutes. The drive from Toronto to Ottawa takes hours. So the drive takes longer.

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. The long hand goes all the way around the clock once. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds. Not 12: there are 12 numbers on the clock, but each one is 5 minutes.)

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
The sand timers are all the same size. 5 sand timers is more than 3. So Owen takes longer.

items.q: Liam claps while he zips up his coat. He claps 12 times. Ava claps 8 times while she zips up her coat. They clap at the same speed. Who is faster?
items.e: Fewer claps means less time. 8 claps is less than 12 claps. So Ava is faster. (Liam has the bigger number, so he took longer.)

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30. (Not 50: an hour is not 100 minutes. Not 6: at half past, the long hand points to the 6, but that is 30 minutes.)

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: a school day, blinking your eyes, recess.
items.e: Blinking takes about 1 second. Recess takes about 15 minutes. A school day takes about 6 hours. So the order is blinking, recess, a school day.

items.q: Which is longer: 50 minutes or 1 hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. 60 is more than 50. So 1 hour is longer.

items.q: Which is longer: half an hour or 40 minutes?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 40 minutes is more than 30 minutes. So 40 minutes is longer. (Half an hour is not 50 minutes.)

items.q: Put these in order from longest to shortest: brushing your teeth, a car trip to the cottage, a sneeze.
items.e: A car trip to the cottage takes hours. Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes. A sneeze takes about 1 second. So the order is car trip, brushing teeth, sneeze.
They both use 4 sand timers, but the timers are not the same. Each big timer takes longer. So Jayden takes longer. (Not the same time: we can only compare counts when the units are the same.)

items.q: Which is longer: 1 minute or 45 seconds?
items.e: 1 minute is 60 seconds. 60 seconds is more than 45 seconds. So 1 minute is longer. (45 is a bigger number than 1, but seconds are much shorter than minutes.)

items.q: Which is the shortest time?
items.e: Seconds are the shortest unit. 30 seconds is less than 1 minute. So 30 seconds is the shortest. (Not 3 minutes: 3 is a smaller number, but 3 minutes is 180 seconds.)

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: Hours are the longest unit here. 2 hours is 120 minutes. 50 minutes and 20 minutes are less than 1 hour. 100 seconds is less than 2 minutes. So 2 hours is the longest. (A big number is not always a long time.)

items.q: Which is longer: 1 hour or 75 minutes?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. 75 minutes is more than 60 minutes. So 75 minutes is longer. (An hour is not 100 minutes.)

items.q: Zoe’s soccer practice is 1 hour. Emma’s swimming lesson is 45 minutes. Which one is shorter?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. 45 minutes is less than 60 minutes. So Emma’s swimming lesson is shorter.

sets.title: Read clocks to the hour and half hour

items.e: The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 3. So it is 3 o’clock: 3:00. (Not 12:15: that mixes up the hands. Not 3:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 7. So it is 7 o’clock: 7:00. (Not 12:35: that mixes up the hands. Not 7:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 9. So it is 9 o’clock: 9:00. (Not 12:45: that mixes up the hands. Not 9:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)

items.q: At 8 o’clock, where does the short hand point?
items.e: At o’clock, the short hand points right at the hour. At 8 o’clock it points to the 8, and the long hand points to the 12.
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 1. So it is 1 o’clock: 1:00. (Not 12:05: that mixes up the hands. Not 1:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 10. So it is 10 o’clock: 10:00. (Not 12:50: that mixes up the hands. Not 10:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 10. So it is 10 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 means o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)

items.q: At half past, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Half past means the long hand has gone half way around the clock. It points to the 6. (Not the 10: that would be 50 minutes, and half an hour is 30 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. So it is half past 2: 2:30. (Not 3:30: the short hand has not reached 3. Not 2:06 or 2:50: half past is 30 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. So it is half past 4: 4:30. (Not 5:30: the short hand has not reached 5. Not 4:06 or 4:50: half past is 30 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. So it is half past 8: 8:30. (Not 9:30: the short hand has not reached 9. Not 8:06 or 8:50: half past is 30 minutes.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 9. That is clock B. Clock A has the hands mixed up. Clock C shows 10 o’clock. Clock D shows half past 9.

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. So it is half past 7. (Not half past 8: the short hand has not reached 8 yet.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. So it is half past 11: 11:30. (Not 12:30: the short hand has not reached 12. Not 11:06 or 11:50: half past is 30 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. So it is half past 1: 1:30. (Not 2:30: the short hand has not reached 2. Not 1:06 or 1:50: half past is 30 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. So it is half past 9: 9:30. (Not 10:30: the short hand has not reached 10. Not 9:06 or 9:50: half past is 30 minutes.)

items.q: At half past 3, where is the short hand?
items.e: In half an hour the short hand moves half way to the next number. At half past 3 it is between 3 and 4. The long hand is on the 6.

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. That is clock C. Clock A shows half past 4. Clock B shows 3 o’clock. Clock D has the hands mixed up.

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. So it is half past 11. (Not half past 12: the short hand has not reached 12 yet.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way around. The short hand is half way between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. That is clock D. Clock A shows half past 3. Clock B has the hands mixed up. Clock C shows 2 o’clock.

sets.title: How long? Hours and half hours

items.e: Count the jumps: 3:00 → 4:00 → 5:00. That is 2 jumps of 1 hour. So it is 2 hours. (Count the jumps, not the numbers.)
Count the jumps: 8:00 → 8:30. That is 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)
Count the jumps: 2:30 → 3:30. That is 1 jump of 1 hour. So it is 1 hour.
Count the jumps: 1:00 → 2:00 → 3:00 → 4:00. That is 3 jumps of 1 hour. So it is 3 hours. (Count the jumps, not the numbers.)

items.q: Hockey practice is from 4:00 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: Count the jumps: 4:00 → 5:00 → 5:30. That is 1 jump of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 1 hour 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)

items.q: How many half hours are in 1 hour?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 30 + 30 = 60 minutes = 1 hour. So 2 half hours make 1 hour.

items.q: The field trip bus leaves at 9:00 a.m. The ride takes 1 hour. What time does the bus get there?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 9:00 → 10:00. The bus gets there at 10:00 a.m. (Not 9:01: 1 hour is not 1 minute. Not 8:00: that goes back in time.)
Count the jumps: 9:00 → 10:00 → 10:30. That is 1 jump of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 1 hour 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)
Count the jumps: 10:30 → 11:00. That is 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)

items.q: Owen’s family is at the beach from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. How long are they at the beach?
items.e: Count the jumps: 1:00 → 2:00 → 3:00 → 4:00. That is 3 jumps of 1 hour. So it is 3 hours. (Count the jumps, not the numbers.)

items.q: A skating lesson starts at 4:00 p.m. It lasts half an hour. What time does it end?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 4:00 and 30 minutes is 4:30 p.m. (Not 4:50: half an hour is not 50 minutes. Not 5:00: that is a whole hour.)
Count the jumps: 4:30 → 5:30 → 6:30 → 7:00. That is 2 jumps of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 2 hours 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)
Count the jumps: 7:00 → 8:00 → 9:00 → 10:00 → 10:30. That is 3 jumps of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 3 hours 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)

items.q: A family movie night is from 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. How long is it?
items.e: Count the jumps: 7:00 → 8:00 → 8:30. That is 1 jump of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 1 hour 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)

items.q: Story time at the library starts at 10:30 a.m. It lasts 1 hour. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 10:30 → 11:30. It ends at 11:30 a.m. (Not 11:00: that adds only half an hour. Not 10:31: 1 hour is not 1 minute.)

items.q: Priya plays at the park from 3:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. How long does she play?
items.e: Count the jumps: 3:30 → 4:30 → 5:00. That is 1 jump of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 1 hour 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)

items.q: Bedtime is 8:00 p.m. Reading time starts half an hour before bedtime. What time does reading time start?
items.e: Count back half an hour (30 minutes) from 8:00. That is 7:30 p.m. (Not 8:30 p.m.: that is after bedtime. Not 7:00 p.m.: that is a whole hour before.)

items.q: The Canada Day party in the park is from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. How long is the party?
items.e: Count the jumps: 11:30 → 12:30 → 1:30 → 2:30. That is 3 jumps of 1 hour. So it is 3 hours.

items.q: The drive to the cottage starts at 9:00 a.m. It takes 3 hours. What time do they get there?
items.e: Add 3 hours, one jump at a time: 9:00 → 10:00 → 11:00 → 12:00. They get there at 12:00 noon. (Not 1:00 p.m.: that counts 9 as a jump too. Not 9:03: 3 hours is not 3 minutes.)

items.q: Mei’s hockey tournament game is from 6:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count the jumps: 6:30 → 7:30 → 8:00. That is 1 jump of 1 hour and 1 jump of half an hour (30 minutes). So it is 1 hour 30 minutes. (Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 50.)

items.q: The oven timer shows how long until the cookies are done. How long is that?
items.e: A timer shows minutes, then a colon, then seconds. 8:00 means 8 minutes and 0 seconds.
The numbers on a stopwatch count by 5s. The hand points to 30, so it shows 30 seconds.

items.q: Recess is 15 minutes long. 10 minutes have passed. How many minutes are left?
items.e: 15 − 10 = 5 minutes left. (Not 25: that adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: Jayden brushes his teeth for 2 minutes in the morning and 2 minutes at night. How long is that each day?
items.e: 2 + 2 = 4 minutes. (Not 4 hours: brushing teeth is quick.)

items.q: Swimming lessons are half an hour long. How many minutes is that?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30 minutes. (Not 50: an hour is not 100 minutes.)
Count by 5s to the number the hand points to: 5, 10, 15, … 45. It shows 45 seconds. (Not 9: 45 is the 9th number, but each number is 5 seconds.)

items.q: Nathan reads for 20 minutes. Then he reads for 15 more minutes. How long does he read?
items.e: 20 + 15 = 35 minutes. 2 tens and 1 ten make 3 tens, and there are 5 ones. (Not 5: that takes away instead of adding.)

items.q: A movie is 1 hour 30 minutes long. How many minutes is that?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 + 30 = 90 minutes. (Not 130: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: In Leah’s hockey league, each period is 15 minutes. A game has 3 periods. How many minutes of hockey is that?
items.e: Add 15 three times: 15 + 15 + 15 = 45 minutes. (Not 18: that is 15 + 3. Not 30: that is only 2 periods.)

items.q: Quiet reading time is 20 minutes. The timer counts down. It shows this now. How many minutes have passed?
items.e: The timer shows 6 minutes left. 20 − 6 = 14 minutes have passed. (Not 6: that is the time left. Not 26: that adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: The Terry Fox Run starts at 10:00 a.m. Emma runs for half an hour. What time does she finish?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 10:00 and 30 minutes is 10:30 a.m. (Not 10:50: half an hour is not 50 minutes.)

items.q: Afternoon recess is 15 minutes. The bell rang 6 minutes ago. How many minutes of recess are left?
items.e: 15 − 6 = 9 minutes. Count back from 15: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9. (Not 21: that adds. Not 10: when you count back, do not count the 15.)

items.q: Hana’s family drives to the cottage. The drive takes 3 hours. They have driven for 1 hour. How much longer is the drive?
items.e: 3 − 1 = 2 hours left. (Not 4: that adds the hour instead of taking it away.)

items.q: On a snow day, Aiden plays outside for 1 hour. Ethan plays outside for 45 minutes. Who plays longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 − 45 = 15. So Aiden plays longer, by 15 minutes. (Not 55: that counts an hour as 100 minutes. Not Ethan: 45 is more than 1, but 1 hour is more than 45 minutes.)

items.q: Lucas practises piano for 25 minutes on Monday and 30 minutes on Tuesday. How many minutes is that?
items.e: 25 + 30 = 55 minutes. 2 tens and 3 tens make 5 tens, and there are 5 ones. (Not 5: that takes away. Not 28: that adds 3, not 3 tens.)

items.q: A loon dives under the water for 45 seconds. Then it dives again for 35 seconds. How many seconds is it under the water in all?
items.e: 45 + 35: 5 ones + 5 ones = 10 ones, which is 1 more ten. 4 tens + 3 tens + 1 ten = 8 tens. So it is 80 seconds. (Not 70: do not forget the new ten. Not 80 minutes: a loon dive is not that long.)

items.q: The bus ride to the farm takes 40 minutes. The ride back takes 40 minutes too. How long are they on the bus?
items.e: 40 + 40 = 80 minutes. 1 hour is 60 minutes, and 80 is more than 60. So it is 80 minutes, more than 1 hour. (An hour is not 100 minutes.)

items.q: Lunch is 40 minutes. Students eat for 20 minutes. Then they play outside for the rest of lunch. How many minutes do they play outside?
items.e: 40 − 20 = 20 minutes. (Not 60: that adds. Not 40: that is the whole lunch.)

items.q: Kai sets a timer for 12 minutes to tidy his room. The timer counts down. It shows this now. How many minutes has he been tidying?
items.e: The timer shows 7 minutes left. 12 − 7 = 5 minutes. Count up from 7: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 is 5 jumps. (Not 7: that is the time left. Not 19: that adds.)

items.q: Each school day has a 15-minute morning recess, a 40-minute lunch and a 15-minute afternoon recess. How many minutes is that in all?
items.e: 15 + 15 = 30. 30 + 40 = 70 minutes. (Not 55: that leaves out one recess. Not 60: do not forget the new ten when you add 5 + 5.)
